package_info.package_name: CrowdStrike Falcon Rapid Response Content (Windows Sensor)
package_info.package_versions: Sensor version 7.11 and above (Windows only), Rapid Response Content update from July 19, 2024
package_info.why_malicious: The Rapid Response Content update contained a configuration error that triggered an out-of-bounds memory read in the Falcon Windows sensor, causing mass system crashes (BSOD) globally. While not intentionally malicious, the update's effect was functionally equivalent to a denial-of-service attack, disrupting critical infrastructure and business operations by rendering Windows systems inoperable.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, immediately after the Falcon Windows sensor receives and processes the Rapid Response Content update
execution_context.file_location: In-memory configuration (IPC Template Instance) loaded by the Falcon Windows sensor process
required_permissions: filesystem access (to receive and store configuration updates)
kernel/system memory access (required for sensor operation and to process configuration data)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malformed IPC Template Instance (proprietary configuration data) delivered via Rapid Response Content update, which, when loaded by the Falcon Windows sensor, triggers an out-of-bounds memory read due to unexpected or invalid data structure.
malicious_snippets.code_language: proprietary configuration (interpreted by Falcon sensor engine)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, upon processing the Rapid Response Content update, the sensor loads the malformed IPC Template Instance, which causes the sensor process to perform an out-of-bounds memory read on system memory, resulting in a Windows system crash (BSOD).

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Any configuration or content update that causes a security agent to crash the host system is highly suspicious, especially when deployed globally. The update bypassed expected validation controls, directly leading to mass system instability.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior expects configuration updates to be thoroughly validated and never cause system instability or memory errors. In this case, a validation failure allowed a malformed configuration to be deployed, violating the expectation of safe, robust update mechanisms.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate configuration updates may alter detection logic or telemetry collection, but should always be validated to prevent memory errors or system crashes. No legitimate update should ever result in out-of-bounds memory access or system-wide BSOD.
key_indicators: Out-of-bounds memory access triggered by specific configuration data (IPC Template Instance)
Immediate system crash (BSOD) on Windows hosts after applying the Rapid Response Content update
Sensor process crash logs referencing access violation or memory read errors
Deployment of unvalidated or malformed configuration data to production systems

attack_chain.action: CrowdStrike releases a Rapid Response Content update containing a malformed IPC Template Instance.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensor processes the update on Windows hosts.

attack_chain.action: Sensor loads the new Template Instance at runtime, triggering an out-of-bounds memory read.
attack_chain.leads_to: Windows system crashes (BSOD) on affected hosts.

attack_chain.action: Mass outage across millions of Windows systems; critical infrastructure and business operations disrupted.
attack_chain.leads_to: Incident response and rollback of the faulty update.

behavioral_signatures: Falcon sensor or security agent process crashes immediately after receiving a Rapid Response Content update
Out-of-bounds memory access or access violation errors recorded in Falcon sensor or Windows event logs
Simultaneous or widespread BSOD events on Windows systems correlated with the timing of security content updates
file_indicators: Recent update to Falcon sensor configuration (Rapid Response Content) on disk or in memory
Presence of new or modified IPC Template Instances in Falcon sensor's in-memory configuration
Timestamped configuration files or memory regions updated immediately prior to system crash
network_indicators: Sensor contacting CrowdStrike update servers (e.g., falcon.crowdstrike.com) immediately prior to crash
Spike in outbound update traffic from endpoints followed by abrupt drop in system heartbeat or telemetry
Correlated timing between update delivery and onset of system instability
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Falcon sensor process failures or system crashes (BSOD) immediately following Rapid Response Content updates. Correlate crash events with update timestamps and network activity to CrowdStrike update servers. Analyze Falcon sensor and Windows event logs for out-of-bounds memory access or access violation errors. Implement canary deployments and automated rollback mechanisms to detect and contain faulty updates before wide release. Use endpoint monitoring to flag mass simultaneous crashes following configuration changes.
